Yampil Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Yampil's Jewish community, present from the early 17th century, suffered attacks by Russian, Polish, and Swedish forces alike during the Northern War of 1705–08. It later grew to a majority — 58 percent — by 1897, before declining to 32 percent by 1939. Accounts of the community's wartime fate differ: one describes roughly 1,700 Jews from Yampil and neighboring villages executed in two actions in late 1941 and June 1942, while another says the Jews of Yampil were instead ghettoized into Liakhovets — a discrepancy worth noting rather than resolving. This cemetery, whose category is listed as unfenced despite an official 'demolished' classification, existed by the second half of the 18th century based on epigraphic evidence, though it was never marked on old maps.
